## Example 3.30 · Algebraic interpretation {#fv7-example-3-30a .fv-lesson .sphere-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>Let <span data-math="P"></span> be a variable point in three-dimensional space, and <span data-math="A=(1,2,3)"></span> and <span data-math="B=(3,-1,-3)"></span> such that</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{AP}\cdot\overrightarrow{BP}=0"></span></div><p><strong>a)</strong> Algebraically determine the Cartesian equation and state the centre and radius of the sphere.</p>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 3.30(a) · p. 80</div>

::: {.notes}
OneNote: P=(x,y,z), AP=(x−1,y−2,z−3), BP=(x−3,y+1,z+3). The dot product gives (x−1)(x−3)+(y−2)(y+1)+(z−3)(z+3)=0. Expand: x²+y²+z²−4x−y−8=0. Complete squares: (x−2)²+(y−1/2)²+z²=49/4. Centre (2,1/2,0), radius 7/2. Preserve directions AP and BP; reversing just one gives the negative of the dot product, still zero here, but consistent directions support sound reasoning.
:::
